notes: One run per configuration; the ± figures are spread across evals, not run-to-run variance.
Grading was blind: each grader saw the two outputs as A and B.
Eval 0 (runbook review) carries the whole gap: 10/10 with the skill, 6/10 without. The baseline misses the missing audience, the ambiguous pronoun, contract-first ordering and concrete rewrites.
Eval 1 (README for a new hire) separates by 2: the baseline never names its reader and uses one-word headings.
Eval 3 (spec opening) is non-discriminating: 7/7 both ways.
Eval 2 (ship decision) goes the wrong way, 6/8 with the skill vs 7/8 without: the skill run ended on an offer to investigate. Both kept the unexplained three-component list.

Eval 4 (incident reply) ties at 9/10 but is contaminated: reader-contract.md now holds a worked reply built from this fixture. The skill run's one failure, placing the evicted api-server pods on general-b-7, repeats an inference in that worked example. That inference has since been removed from the worked example.
Cost: the skill adds about 10k tokens and 7s per run, mostly reading SKILL.md and references.
